Free and open source. Pairs with your phone in one scan.

Works with what you already pay for

Claude Code Codex Cursor Grok Antigravity OpenCode Ollama

Helmy doesn't resell anything. Sign in with the accounts you already have, and Helmy uses them all, one conversation across every one of them.

Helmy chooses

You say what. Helmy figures out how.

For each message, Helmy weighs what it needs against how much room each of your accounts has left. Quick questions can go to free models, and heavy work goes where there is room.

  • No model picker. No effort dial.
  • Two Claude accounts? Helmy takes turns.
  • With Ollama, a model on your Mac answers when you are offline.

Design

Design screens by asking for them.

Ask for an app's screens or a landing page. They show up next to the chat as real pages you can zoom, drag and retype. Point at something and say what to change.

  • Phone, tablet and web sizes. Drag a page to any width.
  • Your edits save to the files, so Helmy sees them.
  • Leave a comment on any element and send it with your message.

In your hand

Take it with you.

Scan a code to pair your phone, and your chats follow you, live. Send a message, approve something or stop a task from wherever you are. Designs open there too, and you can tap from screen to screen.

  • Encrypted with a key only your pairing code has.
  • Works on the same Wi-Fi, or anywhere with Tailscale.
  • Need the Mac itself? Its screen is a tap away.

93%

of permission prompts get approved anyway, according to Anthropic. People stop reading them.

No more allow, allow, allow

It only asks when it matters.

Helmy checks every action against what you asked for. Reading files and editing in the chat's folder just happen, since they can be undone. Anything that leaves your Mac or can't be taken back comes to you as one plain question.

The check sees your messages and the action, never the contents of a web page or a file. Instructions hidden in them can't talk their way past it. Passwords, keys, downloaded scripts and sudo always ask you first.

The vault

Your keys stay out of the chat.

API keys live in your Mac's Keychain or in HashiCorp Vault. Helmy can run things that need them, but only ever sees their names. If a key turns up in the output, it's blanked out. And .env files are off limits.

  • When a key is needed, you type it in a private field, not the chat.
  • Paste a key by accident and Helmy stops it before it goes out.
  • Use the same keys in your own terminal with helmy run.

Open source

Yours to read, change and run.

Helmy is BSD licensed, and its code is on GitHub. There is nothing to pay for. It runs on subscriptions you already have. Don't like something? Change it, or ship your own build.

  • Free. No Helmy account to make.
  • Your chats, files and keys stay on your computer.
  • Nothing you'd want for yourself is held back.
